basis: Cyber Aware Creations editorial judgment. NIST publishes no Subcategory prioritization; any ordering is editorial and this one is ours, not NIST's.
disclaimer: This ordering is a Cyber Aware Creations opinion about where a programme with nothing recorded should start asking. It is not a NIST prioritization, not a maturity path, and not a compliance sequence. It carries the same caveat as the 0-4 tool scale: a practical convention, not doctrine.
informedBy: NIST SP 1300, 'NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0: Small Business Quick-Start Guide' (February 2024). Read in full. Its per-Function Understand / Assess / Prioritize / Communicate bullets are the closest thing NIST publishes to a starting order, and they changed this table — see researchNote.
informedByNote: Read to inform judgment, not redistributed. No mapping table, and no verbatim text, from any source is copied into this file. Where a source's emphasis moved an entry, the movement is recorded below in our own words.
notConsulted: CISA Cross-Sector Cybersecurity Performance Goals 2.0 — a US federal, public-domain, explicitly prioritized subset published with a CSF 2.0 mapping. It was a candidate input and was NOT read when this table was authored, so it has informed nothing here. Reconciling against it is the obvious next revision.
researchNote: Reading SP 1300 changed seven entries, which is the evidence it was actually read rather than cited. Five Subcategories it prioritizes were missing from v1 of this table and were added: ID.AM-07 (it prioritizes inventorying and classifying business data, which v1 omitted entirely while ranking three other inventories); GV.OC-01 and GV.OC-03 (its first governance questions are what the mission is and what the legal, regulatory and contractual obligations are); GV.RM-03 (it prioritizes managing cyber risk alongside other business risk, not beside it); and RC.RP-03 (it treats verifying backup integrity BEFORE restoring as its own act, which is the step that decides whether a backup was real). Two orderings were changed against our prior judgment: PR.AA-03 now precedes PR.AA-01, because SP 1300 singles out multi-factor authentication as the fastest and cheapest protection available and we had it fifth; and DE.CM-09 now precedes DE.CM-01, because endpoint anti-malware is in its priority set and network monitoring is not.
tailRule: Subcategories absent from `rank` sort after every ranked id, in framework order: Function order as the Core defines it, then Category order, then Subcategory id.

rationale.1-4: You cannot rate access, monitoring, or recovery for assets you cannot enumerate. Hardware, software, data and data-flow inventory resolve the most downstream uncertainty per question asked, and they batch into a single conversation. SP 1300 puts it plainly: before you can protect your assets you need to identify them.
rationale.5-10: The controls that most often decide whether an incident is an event or a crisis: who can get in, is multi-factor authentication actually on, is software patched, is the build known, and is there a backup. Multi-factor leads because it is the cheapest large reduction in risk available to almost any organization.
rationale.11-16: The highest-consequence yes/no questions, then the harder spectrum ones. Whether backups have been proven restorable, and whether a recovery plan and an incident response plan exist and have been exercised, are each answerable in a sentence, and a 'no' is immediately actionable. How good detection is, by contrast, is a matter of degree and a much longer conversation — so it is asked second, not because it matters less but because it costs more to answer. This is a question-ordering, not a dependency-ordering: detection obviously precedes response operationally.
rationale.17-28: Governance, supplier context, and the risk inputs that feed them. Placed after the operational floor deliberately: a CISO with nothing recorded gets more from knowing what they run than from restating who is accountable, and questions about accountability, obligations, supplier exposure, vulnerability identification and awareness are all easier to answer once the operational picture exists.
rationale.29-37: Everything that sharpens the picture rather than establishing it: data protection specifics, incident containment and communication, asset criticality, physical access, and the review-and-improve loop. Real work, all of it — but a programme that answered 1-28 already has a defensible profile, and these refine it.
